p:cNvPr.descr: Two diagrams showing the 3-D structure and surface structures of a yeast tRNAphe. a) The first diagram, on the left, shows the dimensions and parts of the tRNAphe. Its structure is somewhat like that of a DNA double helix, but it twists and is not linear. The structure resembles a ladder, with some nucleotides which are not quite connected. The regions of the tRNA are bracketed and labeled; the residues are numbered. We will begin at residue 1 at the top right section of the molecule. This section is bracketed and labeled "amino acid arm" at the top. It consists of a twisted green section, at the top of which is residue 1. Immediately to the right is the 5' end; the other strand is the 3' end. The 3' end is purple, and has a blue sphere bonded to its end labeled AA, for amino acid. Immediately below this point is residue 72. Continuing down the green section of the tRNA, there is residue 69. The green portion of the molecule continues down its length. After residue 69, the molecule twists, and there is a vertical portion with no nucleotides, only the backbones, residue 7 is labeled on the right. The backbone of the 3' strand, on the right, connects on the right with an orange region, which twists backward, away from the viewer, and up to the left. The orange region has residue 12 labeled on the right. This section, with the green backbone and the orange section, is bracketed and labeled "D arm (residues 10-25)" on the left. The green section continues down, with residue 44 labeled on the left just as nucleotide "rungs" appear. The point on the right where the orange section meets the green section is residue 26. The green section continues to twist downward, completing a full twist before ending in a triangular shape. Partial nucleotide bonds are visible here. The left side of the triangle has residue 32; the right side is labeled residue 38. This whole section is bracketed and labeled on the left "anticodon arm." The anticodon itself is a short yellow section which is part of the bottom right area of the triangle. It is bracketed and labeled "anticodon" on the right. Returning to the orange strand in the middle of the tRNA, it also attaches upward to a blue region, which contains residues 56, 54, and 64. It is labeled the T phi C arm. It is arranged horizontally and twists once before connecting on the right with the green region, right next to the amino acid arm. (b) The 3-D surface model of tRNAphe. The L-shape is more evident with this model. The purple region of the amino acid arm begins at the top right, which is one end of the L shape. It is narrow and is labeled 3'. On top, to the left, the 5' end is labeled. To the left of the purple region begins the large green region, which continues throughout the length of the molecule. The green section continues left, then twists downward and slightly left. Above it is the large blue region labeled the T phi C arm. It makes up the corner of the L shape. Below it, and to the left and right of the green region, there are smaller orange regions. The orange region on the left is labeled the D arm. In between the two orange regions, the green region continues downward, getting wider towards the end of the molecule. This wider green section is labeled "anticodon arm" on the right. At the bottom right tip, there is a small yellow section bracketed and labeled "anticodon."
